This is recorded plainly in both the JSON verdict and the .md.

I did not open the sealed key at corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/artifacts/W1-VISUAL-BLIND-PROTOCOL-A-r2/SEALED-KEY-DO-NOT-OPEN-UNTIL-JUDGED/ — not the mappings, not PAIRING-KEY.json, not pairing-r2.json. The reveal table in the verdict is the decode already supplied in the dispatch brief; only COMMITMENT.json and SEAL-README.md (procedural, decode-free) were read.

I did not independently re-derive the F1/F2/F3 instrument figures (orphaned-material count 321/422 -> 0, contact-junction ratio 0.722, ambient lift +0.631). They are quoted from I3-PROTOCOL-A-R2-RESULT.json, the file the dispatch brief designated as this task's source, and are flagged as such in the verdict rather than presented as independently checked.
I cannot confirm zero re-asks/discards for round 2 with r1's level of certainty — only that none is reported in the source file. Recorded as an inference from absence, not a positive confirmation.

gap_closure[] for GAP-W1-pbr-material-set-unbound was written into the verdict but tools/gap-ledger.mjs ignores it: the ledger only accepts a closure from a LATER wave's critic, and this verdict is wave 1 like the gap that opened it (the same rule silently ignores dozens of other same-wave r2/r3/r4 closures elsewhere in this corpus, so this is an existing corpus convention, not a defect I introduced). The re-measurement is still on record inside the verdict JSON itself for any reader who opens it directly.
